vision: Run battle-tested npm packages on the BEAM via QuickBEAM — no Node.js required.

cross_validation.description: Cross-validation against canonical JS and utility libraries

eth_tools.description: Ethereum JS tools loaded via QuickBEAM (solc, Uniswap, DeFiSaver, 1inch)

foundation.description: QuickBEAM runtime lifecycle, npm setup, browser stubs

v0_3.name: First real npm library end-to-end
v0_3.description: Proves an npm Ethereum library can be installed, loaded and driven from Elixir through QuickBEAM with no Node.js on the host — solc-js is the first consumer that has to work for real.

v0_4.name: The JS library shelf
v0_4.description: Proves the bridge generalizes past one library — that unmodified DeFi SDKs (Uniswap, DeFiSaver, 1inch) and utility libraries (aave math-utils, merkletreejs) run on the BEAM through the same loading contract solc-js proved out.

task.title: QuickBEAM foundation
acceptance_criteria: A public onchain_js function installs an npm package (via the `npm` dep, no Node.js on the host) and loads its browser bundle into a running runtime.

An integration test installs a real package from the npm registry, loads its bundle, and calls one of its exported functions — asserting the returned value's domain meaning, not merely that a call succeeded.
A bundle that fails to load (missing package, syntax error, missing browser global) returns a tagged error carrying the underlying JS/npm message; nothing is swallowed.
`start_link/1` returns a runtime whose JS context persists across `eval/2` and `call/3`; `stop/1` frees it and the process exits.
`apply_browser_stubs/1` makes `self === globalThis` and `window === globalThis` true, and defines `navigator.userAgent` and `location.protocol`.
`OnchainJs.RuntimeSupervisor` is started by the application supervision tree; `DynamicSupervisor.start_child/2` spawns a runtime and `terminate_child/2` stops it.
Where installed packages live on disk, and how a consuming app pins versions, is documented in the module docs and README.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Wrappers for any specific library (solc, Uniswap, DeFiSaver, 1inch, aave math-utils, merkletreejs) — Tasks 2–7.
Runtime pooling / concurrency (`QuickBEAM.Pool`, `ContextPool`) — deferred until a real consumer shows the single-runtime path is too slow.
task.body:
Add quickbeam + npm deps. Create `OnchainJs.Runtime` module with runtime lifecycle management: start with browser stubs, load bundles, supervised runtime in application tree. Include integration test that starts a runtime, evaluates JS, and stops cleanly.

Runtime lifecycle, npm setup, browser stubs — [INE-51](https://linear.app/inetpeople/issue/INE-51).

**State as of 2026-08-18** (verified by reading `lib/` and `test/`): the runtime
lifecycle, browser stubs, `RuntimeSupervisor` and the integration test are
implemented and committed. The `npm` dependency is declared in `mix.exs` but is
referenced nowhere in `lib/` — **bundle loading is the remaining, and blocking,
facet**: every one of Tasks 2–7 begins with "install npm package X and load its
browser bundle into a runtime", and there is currently no public function that
does either. Dispatch trigger: this defines the public loading contract the rest
of the roadmap builds on, and it needs live evidence against the real npm registry.

task.title: solc-js compilation (.sol → ABI + bytecode)
acceptance_criteria: `OnchainJs.Solc.compile/2` accepts `.sol` source and returns `{:ok, %{abi: [...], bytecode: "0x..."}}` for a real contract, with bytecode that is non-empty, even-length hex.
The returned ABI's function entries match the contract's declared external/public functions by name and signature — asserted against a fixture contract, not just checked for shape.
Compiler version, optimizer settings and EVM version are caller-supplied parameters surfaced in the result; no solc version, optimizer run count or EVM version is hardcoded as a module constant.
A contract with a compile error returns a tagged error carrying solc's own diagnostic (message, severity, source location); warnings are surfaced rather than discarded.
An integration test compiles a contract that exercises a constructor with arguments, and pins the creation-bytecode/runtime-bytecode distinction so callers know which one they receive.
The handoff to `Onchain.Sleuth.query/3` (creation bytecode taken directly) is shown by a documented example or an integration test.
solc-js version is pinned in a committed npm manifest; the pinned version is reproducible from a clean checkout.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Deploying the compiled bytecode or signing transactions — that belongs to onchain / onchain_evm.
Solidity source generation (codegen) — onchain_evm owns it.
Multi-file projects with import remappings, unless they fall out of Standard JSON for free.
task.body:
Load solc-js via QuickBEAM, expose `OnchainJs.Solc.compile/2` that takes `.sol` source and returns `{:ok, %{abi: [...], bytecode: "0x..."}}`. Two consumers:

- **onchain_evm codegen pipeline** — generate `.sol` → compile to bytecode → deploy via Signer.
- **onchain Sleuth** (see onchain/ROADMAP.md Task 62) — compile a custom read-only `.sol` query to bytecode, hand off to `Onchain.Sleuth.query/3` which ships it in an `eth_call` for one-shot execution against live chain state.

Both paths use the same output (`bytecode` field). Sleuth takes the creation bytecode directly; deployment flows prepend it with constructor args and send via Signer.

Closes codegen pipeline; also feeds onchain Sleuth.

**Authority:** the Solidity compiler's own Standard JSON input/output contract
(solidity docs / solc-js) defines semantics here. Third-party Elixir or JS
wrappers are reference material only and never override it. Drive solc through
Standard JSON rather than the legacy string API, so optimizer settings, EVM
version and output selection are expressible.

Dispatch trigger: EVM bytecode is the deliverable, it is a public contract two
other repos consume, and correctness needs evidence from the real compiler.

task.title: Uniswap v3 SDK routing (optimal swap paths, price impact)
acceptance_criteria: `OnchainJs.Uniswap.route/4` returns a route for a real, liquid mainnet pair: the path's token sequence starts at the input token and ends at the output token, the quoted output amount is non-zero, and price impact is returned as a bounded percentage.
The route is produced by the Uniswap SDK running in a QuickBEAM runtime — not reimplemented in Elixir.
One relevant real error is pinned by an integration test (no route / insufficient liquidity for an illiquid pair) and returns a tagged error tuple, never nil or an empty list presented as success.
Chain id, RPC endpoint and slippage tolerance are caller-supplied; no chain id, router address or fee tier is hardcoded.
Missing RPC credentials make the integration test flunk with the exact env var names and `export` commands — never a silent skip.
Multi-hop routing is exercised by at least one test where the best path is not a direct pair.
SDK versions are pinned in the committed npm manifest.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Executing the swap (signing/sending) — onchain owns transaction submission.
task.body:
Load `@uniswap/v3-sdk` + `@uniswap/smart-order-router` via QuickBEAM. Expose `OnchainJs.Uniswap.route/4` for optimal swap paths. JS SDK handles tick math and multi-hop routing out of the box.

**Authority:** Uniswap's own SDK and its published docs define routing semantics;
the router needs live chain state, so this task cannot be completed against
fixtures alone. Observe at least one real successful route and one real failure
before writing the implementation, then pin both.

Dispatch trigger: correctness depends on live external-system evidence (RPC +
pool state), and the router's chain/provider wiring spans the QuickBEAM bridge
and onchain's RPC layer.

task.title: DeFiSaver recipe builder (@defisaver/sdk)
acceptance_criteria: A public function builds a flash-loan → action-sequence → repay recipe with `@defisaver/sdk` and returns encoded calldata.
The encoded calldata is decoded back in a test and asserted to match the intended action sequence — selector and arguments round-trip — rather than merely asserting a hex string was produced.
Recipes the SDK rejects (unbalanced flash loan, unknown action, wrong argument arity) surface as tagged errors carrying the SDK's own message.
No protocol constant is hardcoded: contract addresses, chain ids, action ids and token decimals come from the SDK or from caller-supplied parameters.
At least one recipe with more than one intermediate action is covered, proving sequencing is preserved in the encoding.
SDK version is pinned in the committed npm manifest.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Simulating or executing the recipe on-chain — onchain_evm (revm) and onchain own that.
task.body:
Load `@defisaver/sdk` via QuickBEAM. Expose recipe construction: flash loan → action sequence → repay, returning encoded calldata.

Flash loan recipes → encoded calldata.

**Authority:** `@defisaver/sdk` and DeFiSaver's own documentation define action
ids, argument encoding and recipe validity. Do not infer encoding from block
explorers or third-party wrappers.

Dispatch trigger: the deliverable is calldata that moves borrowed money — a
mis-encoded action sequence is a fund-loss class of bug, so it needs independent
verification.

task.title: 1inch Fusion SDK (DEX aggregation)
acceptance_criteria: A public function obtains a Fusion quote (and, where the SDK supports it without broadcasting, builds an order) through `@1inch/fusion-sdk` running in a QuickBEAM runtime.

An integration test pins one real successful call, asserting domain meaning — quoted amounts consistent with the requested pair and amount, auction/preset parameters present, order hash of the documented shape — not merely HTTP 200 or `is_map/1`.
One relevant real error from the live API is pinned (unsupported pair, amount below minimum, or invalid key) and returns a tagged error carrying the API's own message and status.
Missing API credentials make the test flunk with the exact env var names, `export` commands, and the URL to obtain a key — never a silent skip.
Chain id and token addresses are caller-supplied; nothing venue-specific is hardcoded.
SDK version is pinned in the committed npm manifest.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Comparing 1inch routes against Uniswap routes (Task 3) — that is a separate consumer concern.
task.body:
Load `@1inch/fusion-sdk` via QuickBEAM. DEX aggregation across multiple protocols. Complement to Task 3.

**Authority:** 1inch's official Fusion SDK and API documentation define the
request/response and error contract. Observe at least one real success and one
real error against the live API before implementing, then pin both.

Dispatch trigger: this is a live external API whose semantics cannot be
established from documentation alone, and it carries credential handling.

task.title: Aave math-utils cross-validation
acceptance_criteria: Property-based tests feed identical inputs to `@aave/math-utils` (in a QuickBEAM runtime) and to onchain_aave's corresponding math functions, and assert agreement.
The comparison tolerance is a named constant with a written rationale tied to fixed-point scaling (ray/wad) and rounding mode — not a value widened until tests passed.
Rounding mode and scaling assumptions are asserted explicitly, since they are the most likely source of divergence.
A genuine divergence fails the test and reports the exact input that produced it; there is no catch-all branch that passes on both outcomes.
At least the core health-factor / borrow-capacity / accrued-interest paths are covered, with the covered set listed in the test module doc.
Any divergence found is written up (task body of a follow-up or the test's failure message names which side is believed wrong and why).
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: Fixing onchain_aave's math — a divergence is reported here and fixed in onchain_aave.
Adding new math functions to onchain_aave.
task.body:
Load `@aave/math-utils` via QuickBEAM and run the same calculations through both JS and onchain_aave's math modules. Property-based tests comparing outputs across implementations.

Validate onchain_aave math against canonical JS.

**Authority:** `@aave/math-utils` is Aave's own published implementation and is
the reference here; where the two disagree, the divergence is a finding to
report, not something to paper over by widening a tolerance.

Dispatch trigger: this grades money math against an independent implementation —
the whole point is that the grader is not the author of onchain_aave's math.

task.title: Merkle proof construction (airdrops, whitelists, storage proofs)
acceptance_criteria: `OnchainJs.Merkle.build_tree/1` returns a root and `prove/2` returns a proof that merkletreejs itself verifies.
A proof produced here verifies under the sorted-pair keccak256 rule used by OpenZeppelin's `MerkleProof`, asserted against a known-root test vector produced independently of this code.
Hash function and pair-sorting are caller-visible options, not hardcoded; a test shows sorted-pair and unsorted-pair trees over the same leaves produce different roots, and the default is documented.
Leaf encoding is explicit and documented (how an address/amount pair becomes a leaf), since a mismatched encoding produces a root nothing on-chain can verify.
Edge cases pinned: single-leaf tree, duplicate leaves, and empty input rejected with a tagged error.
A proof for a leaf not in the tree fails verification and returns a tagged error rather than an empty proof.
merkletreejs version is pinned in the committed npm manifest.

Every public function added here is `Descripex`-annotated with `api()` (params carry `kind`/`description`, `:exchange_data` params carry `source`, and a `returns` is declared); the module is added to `OnchainJs`'s `Descripex.Discoverable` list and to `@annotated` in `test/onchain_js/descripex_test.exs`, whose contract tests must pass.
`mix ci` passes.
out_of_scope: On-chain verification contracts — this produces proofs, it does not deploy verifiers.
Merkle Patricia trie / EIP-1186 storage proofs, which are a different structure than the airdrop-style tree here.
task.body:
Load `merkletreejs` via QuickBEAM. Expose `OnchainJs.Merkle.build_tree/1` and `prove/2` for airdrop claims and storage proofs.

**Authority:** on-chain verification is what makes a proof useful, so the
binding contract is OpenZeppelin's `MerkleProof` convention (keccak256 over
sorted sibling pairs) as documented by OpenZeppelin, plus merkletreejs' own
options documentation. A proof that only verifies inside merkletreejs but not
under the sorted-pair rule is a broken proof.

Dispatch trigger: cryptographic construction where the classic failure — an
unsorted-pair tree that verifies locally and fails on-chain — is silent.
